brief: A compact desk unit with a drawer, plus a spike at a corner where three bases meet to hold a small platform.

requirements.evidence: Four level-0 cells: full bases at (0,0), (1,0), (0,-1) and half base at (-1,0), joined by three joint bolts. check_build: no errors, meshClash clear.
Notch drawer frame (notch:0#1,-1#notch3) fills the empty position at (1,-1) between bases (0,-1) and (1,0). A half-base cut-face drawer was not offered, so the notch drawer was used.

requirements.requirement: Spike at a corner where three bases meet
requirements.evidence: Mount spike spike:0#0,-1|0,0|1,0 at the junction of (0,0), (1,0), (0,-1).

requirements.requirement: Small platform held by the spike
requirements.evidence: setSpikeAccessory platform-sm accepted on that mount spike. It is not a separate node in get_build, so this rests on the accepted op.

finish.summary: Built a 4-cell desk cluster with a notch drawer frame at (1,-1), a mount spike at the three-cell corner (0,0)/(1,0)/(0,-1), and a small platform on the spike. check_build shows no rule errors and meshClash clear.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
